blogPosts.title: How Much Does Attic Storage Cost in Melbourne? 2026 Guide
blogPosts.excerpt: Wondering about attic storage costs for your Southbank home? We break down prices for Essential, Clean-Air, and Premium Attic packages in Melbourne.
body: If you're a Southbank homeowner looking to reclaim your roof space, the first question is usually 'How much will it cost?' Attic storage prices in Melbourne vary depending on the size of your attic, the level of finish, and whether you need extra features like skylights or electrical work. At Ashford Attics, we've been providing transparent quotes for over 20 years, and we know what adds value and what doesn't.

A basic Essential Attic package — particle board flooring and a safe ladder — typically starts around $2,500 to $3,500 for a standard 3x3 metre space. This is perfect if you just need a dry, clean area for boxes and seasonal items. The cost rises if your roof pitch is steep, or if insulation needs to be moved. We always include a fixed written quote so there are no surprises.

The Clean-Air Attic, which adds dust-proof wall lining and kickboards, generally ranges from $4,500 to $6,500. This is the most popular choice for families storing clothing, bedding, or keepsakes. The lining prevents dust from filtering down into your living areas — a huge plus in Melbourne's variable climate, where dust storms and pollen can be an issue.

For a Premium Attic Room with plastered walls and ceiling, paint, optional carpet, skylight, and ventilation, expect to invest from $8,000 to $15,000. It transforms your attic into a usable room — great for a home office, guest space, or hobby room. Many Southbank homes with limited floor area find this far more cost-effective than a full extension.

Additional costs include skylights ($800 to $1,200 each installed), attic ladders ($300 to $800 depending on type), and lighting/powerpoints ($200 to $500). The total depends on the complexity of your roof structure. We always recommend a free on-site measure and quote — that way you get an accurate price based on your actual attic, not an estimate.

One thing to keep in mind: unlike many attic companies, we include a full workmanship guarantee with every installation. So you're not just paying for materials — you're paying for peace of mind. If you're in Southbank or anywhere in Melbourne, give us a call. We'll come out, take a look, and give you a no-obligation price that's fair and fixed.

blogPosts.title: Attic Conversion vs Home Extension: Which Is Better for Your Southbank Home?
blogPosts.excerpt: Should you convert your attic or build an extension? We compare costs, time, and value for Southbank and Melbourne homeowners considering extra space.
body: Southbank homeowners often face a common dilemma: do we convert the attic or add a ground-floor extension? Both add space, but they differ dramatically in cost, disruption, and return on investment. With Melbourne property prices climbing, many are turning to attic conversions as a smarter, faster alternative. Here's what you need to know.

A typical single-storey extension on a Southbank home can cost anywhere from $150,000 to $300,000 and take 6 to 12 months. You'll need council permits, structural engineering, and often temporary accommodation. On the other hand, an attic conversion from Ashford Attics starts at around $4,500 and can be completed in as little as 2 to 5 days, with no structural changes to your home's footprint.

Attic conversions also have minimal disruption. Our team works cleanly, and because we access the roof space without scaffolding (usually), your living areas stay largely untouched. Extensions require excavation, concrete, framing, roofing, and landscaping — weeks of noise and dust. For families in Southbank's tight streets, that can be a nightmare.

From a value standpoint, adding a Premium Attic Room with a skylight can increase your home's usable square footage by up to 30%. While an extension adds more floor area, the cost per square metre is far higher. Moreover, many Melbourne buyers now see attic storage as a premium feature — especially in inner suburbs where space is at a premium.

However, attics are not suitable for every home. If your roof pitch is too low (under 1.5m at the highest point) or if the truss design prevents walkable space, an extension might be the only option. We always do a thorough assessment during your free quote to check headroom, bracing, and access. No pushy sales — just honest advice.

For most Southbank terraces, townhouses, and even some apartments with attic voids, conversion is the clear winner. It's faster, cheaper, and less disruptive. If you're on the fence, call Ashford Attics for a no-obligation look at your roof space. We'll tell you straight up what's possible and what it'll cost.

blogPosts.title: 5 Benefits of a Clean-Air Attic for Melbourne Homes
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover why a Clean-Air Attic is a game-changer for Melbourne homeowners. Dust-proof, protected, and perfect for storing clothes, books, and more.
body: Melbourne's climate is notorious for its rapid changes — one day it's dusty and windy, the next it's humid and rainy. For homeowners who store items in their attic, this can be a problem. Dust, pollen, and moisture can damage belongings over time. That's why the Clean-Air Attic from Ashford Attics has become so popular across Southbank and Melbourne.

The core feature of a Clean-Air Attic is the dust-proof wall lining. This is a heavy-duty barrier that seals the attic from the rest of the roof cavity. Unlike a standard attic where dust and fibres can filter through, a Clean-Air Attic keeps your stored items clean. It's ideal for storing off-season clothing, blankets, books, and even Christmas decorations without them getting coated in grime.

In addition to the wall lining, we install kickboards — raised edges around the perimeter — that prevent items from sliding into the eaves. This also stops any loose insulation from entering the storage area. For families with allergies, this is a huge plus. The sealed environment reduces the circulation of airborne particles.

A Clean-Air Attic also adds structural bracing in some cases, improving the overall integrity of your roof. The battening we install to hold the lining adds extra stability. And because everything is done to Australian building standards, you can rest assured it's safe and compliant. We've installed hundreds of these across Melbourne, from Southbank townhouses to St Kilda apartments.

Another benefit is that a Clean-Air Attic makes future access easier. The lining creates a defined room-like space, so you can walk around, find things, and even add shelving. We often install lighting and powerpoints at the same time, turning a dusty void into a fully usable storage room. It's a small investment that transforms how you use your home.

The cost is surprisingly affordable — typically between $4,500 and $6,500 for a standard attic, including the ladder. When you compare that to renting a storage unit (which can cost $200 a month), it pays for itself in two years. Plus, you get the convenience of having everything at home. If you're in Southbank or nearby, get a free quote today and see how clean your attic can be.

blogPosts.title: Can You Add a Skylight to Your Attic in Southbank? Everything You Need to Know
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking about adding a skylight to your attic conversion in Southbank? We cover costs, council rules, and how it transforms your space.
body: Skylights are one of the most requested features in attic conversions. They bring in natural light, reduce the need for artificial lighting, and make the space feel larger and more inviting. But can you add a skylight to an attic in Southbank? The answer is yes — with a few considerations. Here's everything you need to know.

First, the structure of your roof needs to be suitable. Most Southbank homes have tiled roofs with timber rafters, which can accommodate a skylight between rafters. If your roof has steel trusses or a flat design, a custom flashing kit may be needed. At Ashford Attics, we assess this during your free quote and recommend the best skylight type — fixed or vented.

Council approval is rarely required for a standard skylight installation in a non-heritage area of Southbank, as long as you're not altering the roof structure significantly. However, if your home is in a heritage overlay or if the skylight protrudes above the roofline, you may need a building permit. We handle all the compliance checks so you don't have to.

The cost of adding a skylight to your attic typically ranges from $800 to $1,200 installed, depending on the size (standard 50x60cm), the type of roof tile, and whether you want an opening vent. A vented skylight is great for Melbourne's summers, allowing hot air to escape and helping cool the attic. We also install solar-powered models that are energy-efficient.

In our Premium Attic Room package, a skylight comes as an optional upgrade and makes the room feel huge. We've done several in Southbank's older Victorian terraces where the attic was dark and cramped — after a skylight and plastered walls, it became a bright, usable bedroom. One client turned theirs into a home office with a view of the city skyline.

If you're considering a skylight, think about orientation. North-facing brings in consistent light; south-facing gives soft, even light ideal for artwork. Our team will advise on placement during the site visit. And remember, a skylight works best when combined with good ventilation and insulation. We recommend adding air vents to prevent condensation. Ready to brighten your Southbank attic? Call Ashford Attics for a quote.
